ideas.name: Treasury Auction Price Pressure
ideas.claim: Existing Treasury note prices tend to decline before auctions and recover afterward.
ideas.quote: The yield of 2-year notes increases, on average, by 2.53 basis points during the 5-day period before the auctions, and decreases by 2.32 basis points during the 5-day period afterward.
ideas.mechanism: Anticipated auction supply and dealer hedging create temporary price pressure in secondary Treasury markets.

rules.market: On-the-run US 2-year Treasury notes around 2-year note auctions
rules.timeframe: Five days before and five days after the auction

ideas.claimed_result: The five-day pre-auction return was on average 8.89 basis points lower than the five-day post-auction return for the same 2-year note.
required_data: Historical prices or yields for the same on-the-run 2-year Treasury notes across each auction
